<script>
// Build a TOC from H2/H3 headings (skip the hero H1)
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function(){
  var list = document.getElementById('floating-toc-list');
  if (!list) return;
  var headings = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('h2, h3'));
  headings = headings.filter(function(h){ return !h.closest('.toc-ignore'); });
  headings.forEach(function(h){
    if (!h.id) {
      var id = h.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^\w]+/g,'-').replace(/(^-|-$)/g,'');
      if (!id) id = 'section-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8);
      var base = id, k = 2;
      while (document.getElementById(id)) { id = base + '-' + k++; }
      h.id = id;
    }
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    if (h.tagName === 'H3') li.className = 'h3';
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = '#' + h.id;
    a.textContent = h.textContent;
    li.appendChild(a);
    list.appendChild(li);
  });
});
</script>

## Brief bio

---

Hien Nguyen holds dual positions as an Associate Professor at La Trobe University in Australia and a Professor at the Institute of Mathematics for Industry at Kyushu University in Japan. His role supports research collaboration between the two institutions in mathematical and computational statistics and their applications. He is also Deputy Director of La Trobe's Centre for Technology Infusion. Hien holds an Honorary Associate Professorship at the University of Queensland in Brisbane, Australia, where he continues to supervise students.

Hien's research concerns computational statistics and its connections with machine learning and AI. He studies finite mixture and mixture-of-experts models, Bayesian inference, variational approximation, model selection and stochastic optimisation. His work includes methods for large datasets acquired incrementally or too large for conventional computers, as well as statistical tools for choosing between models and quantifying uncertainty in inferential decisions.

Hien's methods have found applications in neuroimaging, agriculture, genetics and genomics, proteomics, quantum computing, economics, public policy, and social sciences. He holds editorial roles with the *Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics*, *Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics*, *Heliyon Mathematics*, the *International Journal of Mathematics for Industry*, and *Statistical Analysis and Data Mining*.

In his free time, Hien Nguyen enjoys bushwalking and spending time with his three cats: Nyx, Penelope, and Beau.

**Australia’s Economic Accelerator (AEA) Innovate Program IV240100099 (with Aniruddha Desai, Krishnakumar Santhanam, Lalit Yagnik, Mark Jois, Erik van Vulpen, Aidin Bervan, Shanmuga Sundar Dhanabalan, and Phat Huynh): Fully integrated digital technology solution for enhanced dairy farm management.**

*2026–2028*

* This project develops a fully integrated digital technology solution for enhanced dairy farm management.

**SpectraResist-AI (LISAF/LBS/SCEMS Seed Funding, La Trobe University; with Ali Zia, Ali Bajwa, Taseer Ahmad, Ing Kong, Nadeem Shuakat, Wei Xiang, and Ernesto Valenzuela Dominguez): Fine-Grained Spectral Intelligence for Early Herbicide-Resistance Detection.**

*2026–2027*

**ARC DP250100860 (with Shu-Kay Angus Ng, Griffith University; Florence Forbes, Inria; Liming Xiang, Nanyang Technological University): Advancing statistical models for clustering data with structured dependence.**

*2025–2027*

* This project develops statistical models and algorithms for clustering data with structured dependence.

**STARFISH Activity (with Rebecca Chisholm, Mark Davies, Tim Barnett, David Price, Trish Campbell, and Joel Miller): Optimising targeted investigations of Strep A transmission and Environmental Health Initiatives (EHIs) assessment: a model-based approach.**

*2024–2026*

* This project develops model-based methods for targeted investigations of Strep A transmission and Environmental Health Initiatives assessment.

**Inria Associate Teams WOMBAT (with Florence Forbes, Inria): Variance-reduced Optimization Methods and Bayesian Approximation Techniques for scalable inference.**

*2023–2026*

* This project develops variance-reduced optimisation methods and Bayesian approximation techniques for scalable inference.

### Earlier projects

**ARC DP230100905 (with Xin Guo, University of Queensland; Florence Forbes, Inria; Gersende Fort, CNRS): Stochastic majorization–minimization algorithms for data science.**

*2023–2025*

**Australian Government Road Safety Innovation Fund (with Long Truong, La Trobe University): Development of planning-stage crash prediction tools for use at the planning stages.**

*2021–2023*

* This project developed planning-stage crash prediction tools for use in transport planning.

**Inria Associate Teams LANDER (with Florence Forbes, Inria): Latent analysis, adversarial networks, and DimEnsionality Reduction.**

*2019–2021*

* This project supported collaborative work on latent analysis, adversarial networks, and dimensionality reduction.

**ARC DP180101192 (with Geoffrey McLachlan, University of Queensland; and Sharon Lee, University of Queensland): Classification methods for providing personalised and class decisions.**

*2018–2021*

* This project developed classification methods for providing personalised and class decisions.

**ARC DE170101134: Feasible algorithms for big inference.**

*2017–2020*

<style>
  .self-name { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; }
</style>

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  // Process text once so that names are never nested or link markup changed.
  const namePattern = /\b(?:Nguyen,\s*Hien\s+D(?:uy)?\.?(?!\w)|Nguyen,\s*H\.?\s*D\.?(?!\w)|Nguyen,\s*H\.?(?![\w.]|\s*[A-Z])|Hien\s+Duy\s+Nguyen\b|Nguyen\s+HD\b)/g;
  const entries = document.querySelectorAll('#refs .csl-entry, #preprint-entries p');
  entries.forEach(entry => {
    const walker = document.createTreeWalker(entry, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
    const nodes = [];
    while (walker.nextNode()) {
      if (!walker.currentNode.parentElement.closest('a, .self-name')) nodes.push(walker.currentNode);
    }
    nodes.forEach(node => {
      const text = node.textContent;
      const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment();
      let previous = 0;
      for (const match of text.matchAll(namePattern)) {
        fragment.appendChild(document.createTextNode(text.slice(previous, match.index)));
        const span = document.createElement('span');
        span.className = 'self-name';
        span.textContent = match[0];
        fragment.appendChild(span);
        previous = match.index + match[0].length;
      }
      if (previous) {
        fragment.appendChild(document.createTextNode(text.slice(previous)));
        node.replaceWith(fragment);
      }
    });
  });
});
</script>
